ai.description: The Delhi rock gecko (Gekkonidae) reaches 5–6 cm. It is pale grey with dark, wavy transverse bands and a granular dorsal texture. Distinctive features include slender, non-dilated digits and a tail base.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Cyrtopodion aravallense* is best distinguished by the presence of 12–14 longitudinal rows of enlarged, trihedral tubercles on its back, which are notably larger than the scales.
ai.habitat: *Cyrtopodion aravallense* inhabits the rocky outcrops and scrub forests of the Aravalli Range, typically found at elevations between 200 and 600 meters.
ai.behavior: The Delhi rock gecko is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to forage for small insects and arthropods on rocky surfaces and walls.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Cyrtopodion aravallense* is oviparous, typically laying a clutch of two hard-shelled eggs. Breeding occurs during the warmer months, primarily from April to June.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Cyrtopodion aravallense* is endemic to the Aravalli Range in Rajasthan and Haryana, India, typically inhabiting rocky outcrops at elevations between 200 and 800 meters.
